transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-11-05 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~45m | Attendees: Avery Chen, Samir Patel, Maria Gomez, Ethan Cole, Priya Singh

Summary: quick hosted API walk-through focused on chat/text generation basics — streaming, core params (temperature, max_tokens, top_p), and retry/idempotency patterns. Customer evaluating hosted vs dedicated; main concerns are latency, cost, and security (SOC2, SSO).

Topics: API overview, streaming demo, parameter tuning, retry semantics, SDKs and examples, next steps for POC/benchmarks

-- Transcript --
[00:00] Avery Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Avery from Redwood, i;ll hand over to Samir for the demo in a sec.
[00:23] Maria Gomez: hi, yes thanks — quick agenda, we're primarily interested in chat flows, streaming so we can show progressive UI, and how to control cost.
[01:05] Samir Patel: cool, yeah so i'll share my screen — we're focusing on hosted API, chat endpoints, and three things: streaming, params, and retries. I'll start with a basic chat request. (screen share noise)
[02:00] Samir Patel: Example payload: model, messages array, temperature, max_tokens. For streaming we use chunked responses over the same connection — you get tokens as they arrive. Note: make sure to set stream=true and handle partial JSON pieces on the client.
[05:15] Ethan Cole: is there a recommended way for reconnects? like if our web socket drops mid-stream, can we resume?
[05:45] Samir Patel: good question. Hosted API doesn't do full rewind/resume of a stream, so we advise idempotency keys on the top-level request and client-side heuristics: either re-ask with the same idempotency token for non-authoritative writes or fall back to fetching full completion. We also have short-term KV cache/prefix caching for repeated prompts but that is more of a runtime optimization — sometimes the transcript reads that as K V cash, so ignore that typo in the docs.
[08:10] Maria Gomez: so idempotency token stops duplicate charges if we retry?
[08:40] Avery Chen: yeah, correct — idempotency token (client-provided) makes the request dedup within a window, so retries are safe within that window. We also recommend exponential backoff with jitter for transient 5xx errors; for 429s preferrable is to respect Retry-After header.
[12:00] Samir Patel: let's show param tuning: temperature controls randomness, max_tokens caps generation length, top_p for nucleus sampling, and presence/ frequency penalties for repetition. For deterministic systems you set temp=0 and lower top_p.
[15:20] Priya Singh: what about streaming + partial safety? if we stream out tokens and then later abort due to policy checks, how do we reconcile?
[15:45] Samir Patel: pragmatic approach: run safety checks server-side before commit or run them in parallel. For sensitive content we suggest server-side moderation endpoints (we provide a moderation guide) and on the client treat early stream tokens as provisional until final 'done' event.
[18:30] Ethan Cole: cost question, how is streaming billed? per token generated or per response?
[19:00] Avery Chen: billed per token — streaming doesn't change billing semantics, it's just delivery. So you still pay for the same generated tokens. We can show per-route token breakdowns in the Console.
[20:30] Samir Patel: demo time: live code snippet in curl and SDK. (typing) curl -X POST /v1/chat/completions -d '{"model":"rwd-2-small","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Summarize..."}],"stream":true,"temperature":0.7}' — response will be a series of data: chunks that you parse.
[22:10] Maria Gomez: do you have official SDKs for JS/Python?
[22:25] Avery Chen: yes JS + Python + go community SDKs. We also have examples for streaming in the JS SDK showing EventSource and handling partial payloads.
[24:40] Samir Patel: now retries — common pattern: for idempotent read-like requests you can safely retry. For chat sessions with state you should include the entire message history or a session ID that the backend can rehydrate. For long-running sessions, consider saving conversation context in your store and send minimal context to reduce tokens.
[27:00] Ethan Cole: latency concerns — we're in EU, what regions do you operate?
[27:20] Avery Chen: hosted API regions include NA/EU currently and more coming; we route to the nearest region by default. For strict latency SLOs we recommend Dedicated or Private, but many customers do fine with hosted.
[30:00] Priya Singh: security — SOC2, SSO, encryption, do you persist customer prompts?
[30:30] Avery Chen: short answer: yes, we persist for diagnostics unless opted out — we have retention controls and can disable logging for sensitive workloads. We are SOC 2 compliant (link shared in chat), support SAML SSO, RBAC, and KMS integrations for keys. We'll send the security pack after this call.
[33:15] Samir Patel: back to streaming: sample UI pattern — optimistic render tokens as they arrive and show a spinner until final event. Show partial confidence or token-level metadata? We don't expose token-level confidences but we do expose total token counts and model latency per chunk. Sometimes the speech recognizer in our notes mis-types "function calling" as "function calling uh" — apologies.
[36:00] Maria Gomez: one more thing — how do you handle rate limiting and bursts?
[36:22] Avery Chen: per-account rate limits, but hosted has burst allowances; for higher needs Dedicated offers configurable autoscaling and guaranteed throughput. Also we surface 429s with Retry-After and have a quota dashboard in Console.
[38:45] Samir Patel: quick walkthrough of retry headers: standard Retry-After, plus our X-Request-ID for tracing. Put that ID in logs so support can correlate. Also we recommend idempotency-key for POST-like generate calls.
[41:10] Ethan Cole: what about model selection for cost vs quality? recommended approach?
[41:35] Avery Chen: use our model catalog — start with smaller models for bulk tasks, A/B test with higher-fidelity ones for critical flows. Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization and batching config too. We'll share a model recommendation doc.
[44:00] Avery Chen: recap & next steps: we will share pricing and security docs, Samir will schedule the POC benchmark run, and Nexus will share dataset sample and SLOs. Thanks all.
[44:30] Maria Gomez: thanks — that's great.

References shared in chat: link: https://redwood.example.com/security-pack (SOC2), link: https://redwood.example.com/pricing-overview, sample benchmark spreadsheet: https://drive.example.com/redwood-benchmarks (note: placeholder links).

Artifacts to send: pricing deck, security pack, sample SDK snippets, benchmark script.

End of transcript.
